Date: 2026-11-28. Task: review-06 §9 T-2 (P2, prose now; implementation
gated on the G0 resume). User blessing on record: L6 was named the
follow-up engine lever in the P11 memo (2026-11-09) and blessed by the
user 2026-11-27; this memo supplies the law amendment text, the proof
obligations, and the gate design. **Prose only — nothing here is
implemented; the amendment lands only with the implementation PR.**

Scope note this memo adds (post-T-1): L6 attacks **per-fit latency on
wide catalogs** (n = samples ≥ hundreds, the `ms_extract` production
shape and the m1s fixture). It buys **nothing on the O5 grid** (96×1
cells — one column, no j to split) and nothing against the parity row,
which T-1 shows is owned by protocol work volume. L6 is the engine
program's honest remaining lever for its own workloads, not a parity
lever.

## 1. What the committed kernel actually is (the surface L6 touches)

The P11 L1-L5 landing left the KL kernel as: per step, a walk over
`KL_BLOCK = 64`-column blocks (`src/rust/engine/src/nmf.rs:134`,
`(0..n).step_by(KL_BLOCK)` at :550 for the H-step walk and :679 for the
W-step walk); within a block, GEMM → fused
ratio → scatter → update, all per-block-program-order; the only
**cross-block couplings** are the two W-step accumulators
`wparts` (m×k) and `hrow` (k), which accumulate each block's
ascending-j contribution **in ascending block order**
(`kl_w_step_core`, `src/rust/engine/src/nmf.rs:661-714`); every other
buffer cell (`wh` block columns, `num`/`rrow` columns, `h` columns) is
touched by exactly one block per step phase. The block grid is a pure
function of n. The H-step (`kl_h_step_core`, :527) has no cross-block
coupling at all after L3's [j][s] `num` layout.

## 2. Why the p11 sketch does not transfer as-is (the review's 1c warning)

The p11 sketch proved **j-disjoint accumulation**: splitting
`matmul_body`'s j-range gives every thread disjoint output columns, so
each cell's ascending-s sequence is untouched. That argument covers the
per-cell products. It does **not** cover the W-step: `wparts` and
`hrow` are true cross-j reductions. A naive thread-split makes their
float summation tree a function of **thread count** (two threads
produce `(ΣA+ΣB)+(ΣC+ΣD)`-class trees; one thread produces
`((ΣA+ΣB)+ΣC)+ΣD`-class trees with different association), which
**breaks the thread-count invariance contract** — outputs would differ
between `threads ∈ {1, N}`, the exact failure class the law exists to
exclude. The sketch is valid only after the reduction tree is pinned.

## 3. The design (one structure, any thread count)

**L6 — disjoint-j in-fit threading, block-grid-pinned reductions.**

- The KL_BLOCK grid stays a pure function of n (unchanged). Threads are
  assigned whole blocks (round-robin); thread count changes only *which
  worker runs a block*, never the block sequence, the per-block program
  order, or the reduction tree.
- `wparts` and `hrow` become **per-block partials** (owned by the
  block's worker, accumulated ascending-j within the block exactly as
  the committed code does), combined **once, sequentially, in ascending
  block order** after the step's barrier, by one owner, through the
  identical left-to-right combine the sequential code performs. The
  float tree is therefore `(Σ_b0 + Σ_b1) + … + Σ_blast` — the committed
  tree — **for every thread count**, including 1. With `threads = 1`
  the code runs the same partials + combine (no fused fast path).
- Step boundaries are barriers (the W-step's GEMM₂ consumes the
  completed H update; iteration i+1 consumes the completed W update) —
  the fit-level program order is byte-preserved; the per-iteration
  objective/trace observer stays sequential and reads only complete
  step states (the trace-face invariance of P10-A is untouched).
- Scratches (KlScratch, partials) become per-pool-call allocations
  threaded through the driver, extending the L4/L5 hoisting discipline;
  no FFI surface change (D12 holds: one entry, one exit).
- The H-step's `den` hoist (`kl_h_step_core`'s W column sums, verified
  against the committed source at `src/rust/engine/src/nmf.rs:541-548`)
  runs before the block walk and is j-independent: it is computed once
  on one worker (or partitioned by s, ascending-i per s) and is
  read-only for the block wave — the H-step blocks are fully disjoint
  given that hoist, which is what makes the H-step the cheap lane and
  the W-step's partial-tree discipline the only hard part.

## 4. Proof obligations (what the implementation PR must discharge)

- **P-O-1 (fixed tree)**: the wparts/hrow summation tree is a pure
  function of n (the KL_BLOCK grid), identical for `threads ∈ {1, N}`.
  Discharge: code identity (single code path) + G1 below.
- **P-O-2 (disjoint writes)**: in every step phase, each shared buffer
  cell has exactly one writer thread (wh/num/rrow/h block columns;
  partials worker-private). Discharge: a code-level write-set audit in
  the PR, asserted by a debug-indexed overlay test (each cell stamped
  with its writer, no double stamps).
- **P-O-3 (happens-before)**: barrier semantics at both step
  boundaries; no worker reads another's in-step state. Discharge:
  structured per-step parallel sections with explicit joins (no
  free-running workers), plus the G2 gate.
- **P-O-4 (interrupt + statelessness)**: workers see only the
  `cancelled` AtomicBool (contract 7); the flag is polled at block
  boundaries; cancellation fails the whole call with the `interrupted`
  topic; no partial state escapes (D12). Discharge: the existing
  interrupt suite extended with an in-fit cancel probe.
- **P-O-5 (EU parity)**: `eu_h_step`'s `num`/`den` are j-disjoint
  (covered by the same scheme); `gww` is an i-reduction on the
  sequential path. If L6 ships for EU, P-O-1..4 repeat; otherwise EU
  stays sequential and says so.

## 5. Law amendment text (to land verbatim with the implementation PR)

**`src/rust/src/replicates.rs` module docs** — after the "Never
parallel" bullet, the amended text reads:

> * Never parallel: the inside of a fit **— except the L6 lane**.
>   `engine::nmf` is a fixed-order sequential kernel; its floating-point
>   accumulation order is part of the frozen numerics contract. The
>   single sanctioned exception is the L6 disjoint-j in-fit lane
>   (engine-internal, `KL_BLOCK`-grid-pinned): threads may distribute
>   whole column blocks within a step **iff** (a) the wparts/hrow
>   reduction tree is the committed left-to-right block combine for
>   every thread count (P-O-1), (b) every shared cell has one writer
>   per phase (P-O-2), (c) step boundaries are barriers (P-O-3), (d)
>   workers see only the cancelled flag (P-O-4), and (e) the
>   thread-count bit-identity gate (G1) holds bit-exact on every
>   guarded workload. The lane is opt-in per call, defaults OFF, rides
>   the per-call pool cap (never exceeds the `msuiter.threads` budget;
>   CRAN limit semantics unchanged), and the fit-level sequence, the
>   trace observer, and every output byte remain thread-count
>   invariant.

**`vignettes/articles/architecture.qmd` contract 6** — the sentence
"**the parallelism exists only between the independent units**
(the replicate/sample/bootstrap), single-threaded within a unit" gains
the clause:

> …single-threaded within a unit **except the L6 in-fit column-block
> lane, which is bit-identity-gated (P-O-1..4 above; the reduction
> tree, not the thread count, defines the float summation order), and
> the thread-count invariance promise is restated to include it: with
> the same seed the outputs for threads∈{1,N} are `identical()` with
> the lane ON or OFF**.

Contract 7 (interrupts) gains: "L6 workers check only the AtomicBool at
block boundaries; the main thread's `R_CheckUserInterrupt` cadence is
unchanged."

## 6. Gate design (the deciding evidence)

- **G1 — thread-count bit-identity (hard, CI)**: for threads ∈ {1, 2,
  3, 8, pool-max}, on every guarded workload: the frozen
  `tests/kl_bit_freeze.rs` vectors (5 shapes + zero cases), the 21
  REP-100 batch-face anchors (bit-pinned), the kernel CLI protocol
  suite (byte-identical transcripts), the trace-face invariance pair
  (Endpoints/Full), and the EU parity shapes. All `identical()` /
  byte-equal. One red bit = the lane does not ship.
- **G2 — scheduling perturbation (hard, CI)**: the threads=4 fit run
  100× under injected yields/descheduling must be byte-stable (catches
  any residual order leak the fixed-tree argument missed).
- **G3 — CRAN/concurrency budget (law)**: in-fit workers are the
  per-call pool's own threads (`msuiter.threads`; `_R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_`
  cap honored); no global pool, no untracked threads.
- **G4 — accuracy travels (D11)**: bit-identity IS the accuracy gate;
  no tolerance re-anchoring is requested or needed (the lane is
  order-preserving by construction).
- **G5 — measured adoption (bench, after G0 resume)**: the differential
  twin microbench reports the lane's gain at the m1s fixture and one
  wide-catalog fixture (n ≥ 1000) with the lane ON vs OFF; the m1s
  bench record updates only through the frozen protocol (warm-up 1 +
  median 3). Expectation, stated honestly: 2-3x at 4 threads on the
  step core for n ≥ 1000 (barrier + combine bound), ~1x below
  n ≈ 256 (blocks < threads), ~1.1-1.2x end-to-end after the objective
  dilution — the same honest accounting as the P11 table.

## 7. What this memo deliberately does not do

No code, no Cargo.toml change (rayon is already in the tree), no law
edit applied, no bench re-run. The implementation PR (post-G0) lands
the §5 amendment text, the P-O discharges, and the G1-G5 evidence
together, or not at all.
